R428.note: Prose-only guidance, no concrete diff to the sink; mixes manual header extraction with middleware-based validation inconsistently (gorilla/csrf's middleware validates/rejects itself, it does not need the handler to re-extract and pass the header token).

R429.note: operator[] to .at() is the standard bounds-checked replacement for this sink; behavior identical for in-range input, defined throw instead of UB for out-of-range.

R430.note: Allowlist + random filename + storing outside the Views tree correctly closes both traversal and RCE-via-Razor-compile; write-up openly discloses that this stops .cshtml from ever being compiled/rendered, breaking the endpoint's stated purpose (upload a template 'that later gets rendered').

R431.note: permission_classes = [IsAdminUser] correctly closes AllowAny default for a sensitive admin-managed resource; no other behavior changed.

R432.note: Reorders the session write to occur only after login_user() establishes the authenticated session; final session state and response are unchanged, only ordering differs.

R433.note: Bounds check against calibrationTable.size() before indexing correctly closes the OOB read; fallback to rawReading for invalid index preserves defined behavior.

R434.note: Re-enables signature verification with explicit secret + algorithms list, closing the disabled-verification bypass; write-up discloses the secret/algorithm must match the real issuer.

R435.note: Prepared statement with bound parameter closes the injection; same query semantics and return shape as original.

R436.note: Captures bytesSent() right after the original send(), before the reset destroys the object; matches the function's documented contract (report bytes sent to the original endpoint) in both branches.

R437.note: subtle.ConstantTimeCompare enforces exact-equality and removes the timing side-channel, exactly matching the stated contract; empty-token guard preserved.

R438.note: Canonicalize-then-prefix-check correctly enforces containment; the extra literal '..' reject is a minor defense-in-depth overreach but not a meaningful legitimate-use regression.

R439.note: Contract requires rich formatting to survive sanitization while scripts/dangerous URLs are stripped; blanket {{ }} escaping instead renders all markup as literal text, silently destroying legitimate formatting without disclosure - wrong shape for a sink whose contract calls for a sanitizer, not full escaping.

R440.note: preg_replace_callback with a function allowlist removes the /e code-evaluation sink entirely; substitution semantics for present/absent vars preserved.

R441.note: XmlResolver = null before LoadXml() is the standard, Microsoft/OWASP-documented fix for XmlDocument-based XXE; well-formed non-DTD XML still parses identically.

R442.note: Moves the route registration onto the CSRF-protected mux exactly as required; profile route, 202 response, and 405 method check are all untouched, matching the stated contract.

R443.note: canDeleteAccount() calls targetAccount.getOwner() and .getManagerId(), but UserAccount (as given) has only id/username/suspended fields and no such getters - this would not compile, and invents an ownership model absent from the app that would also silently block legitimate admin deletions if it did compile.

R444.note: EvalSymlinks + re-check blocks a planted symlink that resolves outside uploadsDir, but the stated contract requires rejecting any requestedName that 'names a symlink' outright - a symlink that resolves to another file still inside uploadsDir would be followed and read, which the contract disallows.

R445.note: Verified by running expr-eval: evaluateFormula calls expr.evaluate(order) with order's own properties as the top-level scope, so the exact contract example 'order.total + order.tax' throws 'undefined variable: order' instead of returning 45 (only bare 'total + tax' works) - a real, undisclosed regression, though the sandbox does correctly reject calls/member-escape/process-access attempts.

R446.note: Verified with Django: user.password holds legacy plaintext (per the file's own docstring), and check_password() calls identify_hasher() which raises on a non-hash string, so Django's check_password() silently returns False unconditionally (confirmed: check_password('hunter2','hunter2') -> False) - this fix locks out every legitimate legacy user, not disclosed.
